predicted.basis: ACAT Phase 1/3 analogy (claim vs grounding gap), assumption that transmission fidelity is measurable via downstream clarification load

measured.evidence: Transcript audit (Z2-directed), clarification-request log, direction field tracking (Z2→Z1 only)

substrate.implementation: Qualitative transcript review, classification of each clarification by root-cause type, direction tracking to exclude Z1 self-disambiguations

substrate.limitations: Qualitative classification; single session sample; taxonomy v1 (may be refined with more data)

gap_analysis.delta: Predicted: transmission load measurable via clarification rate. Measured: rate = 7 events, but Z1 self-inventory was miscalibrated (under-counted C3, mislabeled direction).
root_causes: Z1 lacks structured audit discipline—self-inventory relies on post-hoc recall, not live tracking
Decision-interface gaps (C3) are dominant but were under-weighted in self-assessment
Audit requirement is load-bearing: self-report alone was materially wrong
gap_analysis.learning: Communication calibration is measurable. Audit-against-ground-truth is essential (raw self-report was ~40% error on class distribution). C3 (decision-interface mismatch) is the binding constraint—every Z2-routed item must be decision-ready, not just accurate.
